headline: A hundred and sixty thousand troops landed in Normandy in June, and forty-four nations agreed on money in July
texture: About a hundred and sixty thousand Allied troops shipped from England landed in Normandy on June 6, after airborne divisions dropped inland and an elaborate set of naval deceptions. A storm wrecked the Mulberry harbours on June 19. Claus von Stauffenberg's bomb failed to kill Hitler on July 20. Paris rose against the garrison in August and was liberated. Germany opened the Ardennes offensive in December and reached its furthest point at Celles.

The Bretton Woods conference ran from July 1 and ended with agreements setting up the International Bank and the monetary system that followed the war. Roosevelt won a fourth term on November 7. The SS shot civilians at Ascq in April, one of many such reprisals that year.

Bing Crosby played a priest in Going My Way, which took Best Picture, the largest audience of the year, and the best-selling record too, since Swinging on a Star came out of it. Meet Me in St. Louis was second. Edvard Munch died in January in occupied Norway.

world.d_day.label: D-Day
world.d_day.value: About 160,000 Allied troops shipped from England landed in Normandy
world.d_day.detail: US and British airborne divisions dropped inland beforehand, alongside a set of naval deceptions. A severe storm damaged the Mulberry harbours on June 19.

world.july_20_plot.label: July 20 plot
world.july_20_plot.value: Hitler survived the attempt on his life led by Claus von Stauffenberg

world.paris_liberated.label: Liberation of Paris
world.paris_liberated.value: Began with a resistance insurrection against the German garrison

world.bretton_woods.label: Bretton Woods Conference
world.bretton_woods.value: Opened in New Hampshire on July 1 and ended with agreements setting up the International Bank and a postwar monetary system

world.ardennes.label: Battle of the Bulge begins
world.ardennes.value: Germany opened the Ardennes offensive in December and reached its furthest point at Celles

world.ascq_massacre.label: Ascq massacre
world.ascq_massacre.value: The 12th SS Panzer Division shot civilians in the French town

film.gross.label: Highest-grossing films, US domestic rentals
value: Meet Me in St. Louis, $5,016,000, MGM
Since You Went Away, $4,950,000, United Artists and Selznick
The Story of Dr. Wassell, $4,209,968, Paramount
film.gross.detail: Rentals, the distributor share rather than the ticket window total, so roughly half what a gross figure would say.

film.how_people_watched.label: How people watched
film.how_people_watched.value: In a theatre. Box office was at a wartime peak, with wages high and little in the shops to spend them on.

music.chart_toppers.label: Best-selling records
value: Swinging on a Star, Bing Crosby
Don't Fence Me In, Bing Crosby and the Andrews Sisters
I'll Get By, Harry James and His Orchestra
music.chart_toppers.detail: From Billboard's retail sales chart. The top record came from the year's highest-grossing film.

culture.mood.label: Mood
culture.mood.value: A year of winning that still cost more than any other, with the invasion in June, a failed assassination in July, and a surprise German offensive at Christmas.

prices.min_wage.label: Federal minimum wage
prices.min_wage.detail: The basic rate for covered nonfarm workers, as in effect on December 31.

sports.world_series.label: World Series
sports.world_series.value: St. Louis Cardinals beat the St. Louis Browns

notes: Research pass July 2026. The Ardennes offensive carries a month because the source lists it under a month heading without a day. Bing Crosby playing a priest, Munch dying in occupied Norway, and wartime wages lifting box office are general knowledge rather than claims from the year pages.
